item.title: How Lula defied the odds to win Brazil's presidency
item.description: Against the odds, Lula has staged a stunning political comeback — but winning Brazil's presidency may prove easier than governing a deeply divided nation.

item.title: Rule changes could hinder personal prescription drug imports
item.description: For years, some people have been buying their prescription drugs from pharmacies outside the U.S. But changes are coming to personal import rules that could make that harder to do.

item.title: Here's why the Tampa Bay Rays made it to the World Series
item.description: The World Series moves to Florida for game 3 between the Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers. One reason for the Rays' success is their shrewd trades. More than half their roster came from trades.

item.title: INVASIVE SPECIES ON SCHOOL MENUS
item.description: The Chesapeake Bay, home to blue crabs, striped bass, and other popular seafood, has a new apex predator, the blue catfish. It's invasive and ravenous, growing to more than 100 pounds. But officials hope one of the fish's other qualities might keep it in check: it's delicious.

item.title: Why some Democrats are hoping for midterm help from independent candidates
item.description: Independent candidates say now is the time to increase their numbers on Capitol Hill. And in some races, Democrats see them as their best bet to deny Republicans a majority.

item.title: U.S. influence in Latin America at stake in runoff election in Brazil
item.description: A polarizing presidential election runoff in Latin America's largest economy and biggest democracy pits leftist Lula da Silva's legacy against Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the former Brazilian president.

item.title: An inside look of the massive data center tearing a Wisconsin community apart
item.description: In Port Washington, Wisconsin, there's a data center being built that's as big as 500 football fields. Residents aren't sure if it could save their community or destroy it.
